extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons institutional users and administrators (signing officials, PIs, AAs, AOs, reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutional users on viewing, editing, and managing Institution and Personal Profiles and related modules (FCOI, IAR, Prior Approval) within eRA Commons. Covers role-based access, required fields, file upload rules, and module-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI module abilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCOI module in Commons allows institutional users to initiate and prepare FCOI reports; electronically submit reports and supporting documents as well as annual FCOI reports; receive notification via email upon the submission and receipt of an FCOI; search and view FCOI reports previously submitted through the Commons; revise an Initial 2011 FCOI Report to update FCOI data following completion of the Retrospective Review or to submit a Mitigation Report when bias is found following the completion of a Retrospective Review; access history of actions; assign FCOI access to other Commons users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the module functions according to your assigned Commons role. See the FCOI topic in Commons Online Help or the FCOI External User Guide for step-by-step instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI policy upload requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each organization must upload its Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) policy to eRA Commons for review (effective Nov 12, 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must be in PDF format under 6 MB. After uploading and submitting, NIH staff will review and accept or reject and notify via listed contact methods. See Guide Notice NOT-OD-21-002 and Policy Documents tab for regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCOI policy file upload behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When uploading an FCOI policy file, the file appears with a trash can icon and a download icon; you can delete or view it prior to submission. Only a single file may be uploaded; uploading another PDF replaces the first. If '!Invalid file' appears, the file likely does not meet upload requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drag-and-drop or browse to add the file, then click Submit to send to agency officials. If resubmitting after NIH contacts you, notify the NIH contact of the re-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: IAR reviewer functionality and COI restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet Assisted Review (IAR) lets reviewers submit critiques, preliminary and final scores, and view grant applications and meeting materials via Commons. IAR can enable reviewers to view critiques of others before the meeting unless conflicts of interest exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must hold the IAR role and be enabled for review meeting(s) to access IAR features. Use the IAR online help system for reviewers for detailed steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based access to Institution Profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the Institution Profile is limited by Commons role; not every user has access and only users with the Signing Official (SO) role can edit it. Only SOs see the Policy Documents tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles listed with access include AA, AO, ASST, BO, FSR, PI, POSTDOC, SCIENTIST, SPONSOR, and SO. Confirm your role if expected functionality is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Profile tabs and core content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institution Profile consists of three main tabs/screens: Institution Basic Information, Institutional Assurances and Certifications, and Policy Documents (SO only). Tabs include preferred organization name, SO contact information, UEI, institutional assurances, and email addresses for Notices of Award and other communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigate via the Institution Profile landing page and top navigation. Use related topics for detailed field definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: View vs Edit mode behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: View mode displays profile information read-only; Edit mode makes applicable data editable in text boxes (not all data can be edited). Only SOs can switch to Edit mode for Policy Documents and many Institution Profile screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click Edit to display editable fields, Save All to persist changes, and Discard Changes to revert. Closing a section is not the same as saving—navigating away without clicking Save All will lose edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save All and error-saving semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: To save any profile changes, you must click the Save All button. Save All saves changes made across all sections. If required fields have errors (red/pink with red x), you must fix all errors—if you save while errors exist, changes are NOT saved and an error message appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General errors display at the top of the screen after an attempted save; specific error messages appear adjacent to fields with errors. Fix format and required-field errors (e.g., email must contain '@') before saving.

rubrics_metrics.name: How data errors are indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section has required fields; missing information or wrong format (e.g., email without '@') appears in red font and with error messages. A general error appears at the top after save attempt and specific messages next to erroneous fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review red/pink marked items and correct them. Use the displayed messages to identify exact issues before attempting Save All again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Profile - Profile Name vs Commons Preferred Name
rubrics_metrics.description: The Profile Name is the NIH-designated organization name and is not editable. The Commons Preferred Name, if existing, can be edited by users with the SO role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To edit the Commons Preferred Name, click Edit and update the field, then click Save All. Do not rely on hiding/collapsing sections to persist changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Contact Information required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institution Contact Information component includes required fields: Notice of Award Email, Announcements & Notifications Email, Closeout Correspondence Email, Contact Name (primary contact), Contact Phone, and Contact Email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH uses these emails/contacts for Notices of Award, reminders, closeout communications, and general correspondence. Ensure these are accurate and in the correct format before saving.

rubrics_metrics.name: About the Institution - UEI and opportunity eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary UEI is populated from registration and is not editable through Commons. Secondary UEI(s) can be added/edited/removed by SOs. Opportunity Type Eligibility shows which of three opportunity types the organization can apply for; at least one must be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To add a Secondary UEI, click Add and enter the 12-character UEI; to remove, click Remove and confirm. Opportunity types set at registration are checked and non-editable; if you mark an additional opportunity type and save, you cannot unmark it later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity types enumerated
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three opportunity types: NIH Grants/Contracts (required for NIH funding), Non-NIH Grants/Contracts (for other agencies using NIH eRA systems), and Other Transaction Authority (OTA) opportunities (neither grants nor contracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate opportunity types to expand what your organization can submit for; at least one type must be checked for application eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal-Wide Assurance and Animal Welfare Assurance handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal-Wide Assurance Numbers can be added, edited, and removed by SOs; to add, click Add and enter the number then Save All. Animal Welfare Assurance Number displays the OLAW number and is not editable; old-format numbers may appear in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage Federal-Wide Assurance numbers carefully; use Save All to persist. For Animal Welfare Assurance edits, contact appropriate agency (number is not editable via Commons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Cost Negotiations fields and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indirect Cost Negotiations section displays Negotiator Name and Last Negotiation Date (read-only unless you hold SO role). SOs can edit Negotiator Name and Last Negotiation Date, and the date format must be MM/DD/YYYY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click Edit to modify these fields and Save All to persist. Ensure date format compliance to avoid validation errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing Official (SO) discovery and role importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing Officials (SOs) are the only users who can submit most documentation and reports and can manage/create eRA Commons accounts (alongside AOs and AAs). If you lack an account or cannot log in, you need an SO from your organization to create or reset accounts; contact the eRA Service Desk if you cannot find your SO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Institution Profile Signing Officials pane to view name, phone, and email for SOs after logging in. If unfamiliar with your organization's SO, check the Office of Sponsored Research or similar office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Address required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: When editing Institution Address (SO only), required fields include Street Address, City, Country (select from drop-down), State/Province (select), Zip/Postal Code, and Phone (required). Fax is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate postal and phone information; use Save All to persist edits. Invalid or missing required address fields will trigger error indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Assurances and Certifications status display
rubrics_metrics.description: The Status section displays Office of Research and Integrity Certification Status as either 'Assurance OK' or 'Expired' (expired displays in red). Expiration date displays below the status and is red if expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor expiration dates and update assurances as needed. The Assurances & Certifications list shows read-only check marks and the date of indication for each item; SOs can edit via Edit Assurances and Certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Assurances and Certifications (SO only)
rubrics_metrics.description: SOs can click 'Edit Assurances and Certifications' to check or uncheck certification/assurance indicators; a check-mark indicates compliance. There is an '(explain your answer)' link to provide additional information in a text box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After making changes, click Save All to persist. Unneeded assurances need not be checked; only applicable assurances should be indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of specific assurances and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide lists specific compliance assurances (e.g., Age Discrimination Assurance, Civil Rights Assurance, Handicapped Individuals Assurance, Inclusion of Children Policy, Sex Discrimination Assurance, Women and Minority Inclusion Policy) and research-specific requirements (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov Requirement, Conflict of Interest Assurance, Institutional Debarment Assurance, Human Subjects, Vertebrate Animals, Recombinant DNA and Human Gene Transfer, Research Misconduct, Select Agent Research, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all assurances/certifications apply to every organization. For details consult the Grants Policy Statement (search 'PUBLIC POLICY REQUIREMENTS' or the specific assurance name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Profile editing and save requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Personal Profile is the central repository for individual users; to edit click Edit, make changes, and click Save All. To save changes you must fix ALL error items in red/pink that show a red x—even those unrelated to your current change—or the save will fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections include Name and ID, Demographics, Employment, Reviewer Information, Trainee Information, Education, Reference Letters (PIs), Publications (if applicable), and xTRACT Information. You may delegate authority to maintain your profile to other users in your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Approval module purpose and role permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Policy allows grantees discretion for some changes, but some require written prior approval. The Prior Approval module lets PD/PIs and SOs withdraw a submitted grant application (not yet awarded); SOs can request PD/PI changes, No Cost Extensions (when conditions met), create Carryover requests (SO only), and submit Other Request types (SO only, subject to IC discretion). DMS Request must be used by NIH recipients subject to the DMS Policy to submit revisions to their approved DMS plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access Prior Approval via eRA Commons navigation. Available request types and eligibility criteria are described in individual help topics linked from the module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiating Prior Approval requests and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate a Prior Approval Request: log into eRA Commons, navigate to Prior Approval, select request type from the dropdown and click Go. Search results list all grants under your jurisdiction eligible for the selected request type. Help topics for each request type list eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request is already pending for a grant, a message with the pending request number is shown and you may have the option to initiate another request. SOs have search tools to narrow large result sets; PIs have toggles to narrow fewer grants.
